concepts.label: circuit
concepts.gloss: A circuit is a managed end-to-end transport service or logical connection between hand-off points whose traffic is conveyed over an underlying bearer.
concepts.example: CIR-7 is a New York–Frankfurt transport circuit presented at ho-NY-CIR7 and ho-FRA-CIR7 and carried on the 193.1 THz NY–FRA wavelength.
concepts.evidence: Read from kind “transport-circuit,” relations “presents-at” hand-offs and “carried-on” a bearer, and instance “CIR-7 (NY-FRA)”; distinguished from m.bearer, which is the wavelength that carries the circuit.

concepts.label: hand-off
concepts.gloss: A hand-off is a circuit-specific demarcation point at which a transport circuit is presented to a customer, peer, or adjoining network.
concepts.example: ho-NY-CIR7 is the New York demarcation where CIR-7 is presented, paired with ho-FRA-CIR7 at the Frankfurt end.
concepts.evidence: Read from kind “demarcation-point,” relation “on-circuit,” synonym “circuit hand-off,” and endpoint-like instances “ho-NY-CIR7” and “ho-FRA-CIR7”; ruled out m.circuit because a hand-off is where the circuit is presented, not the connection itself.

concepts.label: rate
concepts.gloss: A rate is the circuit’s specified traffic-carrying capacity, including the applicable commitment basis.
concepts.example: CIR-7 has a committed rate of 5 Gbit/s.
concepts.evidence: Read from kind “rate,” relation “of-circuit,” and instance “5 Gbit/s committed”; distinguished from m.grade because this is a quantified committed capacity rather than a service-class label.

concepts.label: latency
concepts.gloss: Latency is the measured or specified transit delay for a circuit, optionally scoped to a particular path such as its primary path.
concepts.example: The primary path of CIR-7 has a latency of 7.2 ms.
concepts.evidence: Read from kind “latency,” relation “of-circuit,” and instance “7.2 ms (primary path)”; distinguished from m.rate because it measures transit delay rather than capacity.

concepts.label: protection
concepts.gloss: Protection is the resilience scheme assigned to a circuit, describing how redundant transport paths or resources preserve service after a failure.
concepts.example: CIR-7 uses 1+1 path protection, with traffic protected by a concurrently available redundant path.
concepts.evidence: Read from kind “protection,” relation “of-circuit,” and instance “1+1 path protection”; distinguished from m.grade because it specifies a resilience arrangement rather than an overall service tier.

concepts.label: grade
concepts.gloss: A grade is a named service tier assigned to a transport circuit that categorizes its expected service level or assurance, from premium classes to best-effort treatment.
concepts.example: CIR-7 may be assigned the platinum grade to indicate the operator’s highest transport service tier.
concepts.evidence: Read from kind “transport-grade,” relation “of-circuit,” and tier instances “platinum,” “gold,” and “best-effort”; distinguished from m.protection and m.rate because grade classifies the overall transport service level rather than a specific resilience scheme or bandwidth value.

concepts.label: bearer
concepts.gloss: A bearer is an underlying transport resource—here, an optical wavelength—on which one or more circuits are carried between locations.
concepts.example: The 193.1 THz NY–FRA lambda is the bearer that carries CIR-7.
concepts.evidence: Read from kind “bearer,” synonyms “wavelength” and “lambda,” relation “carries” circuit, and instance “lambda 193.1THz NY-FRA”; ruled out m.circuit because the bearer is the underlying wavelength resource carrying the managed circuit.
